title: Zoom in: adding a consumer moves only the partitions that must move
caption: The coordinator reassigns partitions whenever the group changes; the protocol decides how much of the group pauses while it does.

messages.label: JoinGroup
messages.note: Dinner rush: the search group's lag is climbing, so a third indexer starts. The topic has 6 partitions: indexer 1 owns p0–p2, indexer 2 owns p3–p5.

messages.label: rebalance: rejoin
messages.note: With the cooperative protocol, members keep processing what they own while the new assignment is worked out.

messages.label: revoke p2 only
messages.note: Only partitions that move are revoked. p0 and p1 never stop.

messages.label: commit p2, release it
messages.note: Committing first means the next owner starts exactly where indexer 1 stopped.

messages.label: resume from committed offsets
messages.note: Each partition still has exactly one reader in the group. Three readers drain the lag faster.

scenarios.name: Alternative: eager
scenarios.summary: The older eager protocol revokes everything from everyone: simpler, but the whole group stops for every membership change.

messages.label: revoke all: p0–p2
messages.note: Every member gives up every partition, even the ones that won't move.

messages.label: commit, stop, wait
messages.note: Nothing in the group is processed until all members have rejoined. In a 100-member group that pause can last tens of seconds.

scenarios.name: Indexer 2 crashes
scenarios.summary: A dead member is only noticed after the session timeout, and the new owner re-reads from the last commit, so handlers must be idempotent.

messages.label: heartbeat
messages.note: Indexer 2 is killed. Its heartbeats stop arriving.

messages.label: wait for session timeout (45 s)
messages.note: p3–p5 are not being read during this wait, so their lag grows.

messages.label: re-read p3 from last commit
messages.note: Records indexer 2 processed after its last commit are indexed again. The upsert by order id makes that harmless.

scenarios.name: Rolling deploy
scenarios.summary: With static membership a restarting member keeps its partitions, so a deploy doesn't trigger a rebalance per instance.

messages.label: SIGTERM: commit, close
messages.note: Indexer 1 has a fixed group.instance.id, so it doesn't send LeaveGroup on shutdown.

messages.label: hold p0–p2 for indexer-1
messages.note: The coordinator waits up to the session timeout before reassigning anything.

messages.label: JoinGroup as indexer-1
messages.note: The new version is up 20 s later.

messages.label: same partitions: p0–p2
messages.note: Indexers 2 and 3 were never interrupted; only p0–p2 paused, for the length of the restart.
